lines.trans: Thank you for waiting — perhaps I have kept you waiting far too long. Shall we begin?

words.gloss: be known (in かもしれない)

lines.trans: Yes, I look forward to working with you.
Mr Muranishi, are you playing the male lead yourself?! Should the director really step on camera?
Don't worry — speaking in front of an audience has always been my strong suit.
Believe it or not, I used to be the number-one salesman of English conversation sets!

words.reading: エイカイワキョウザイ

words.gram: Past tense of plain copula だ.

lines.trans: What a bizarrely twisted shape that whistle has...
Toshi, this is absolute perfection! Now let's get the camera rolling.
Let's put this prop to brilliant use — please try giving it a blow.
When you begin feeling good, blow it once; when passion builds higher, blow it twice.
And when it becomes utterly irresistible, blow it three times.
That way viewers can tell the exact degree of your emotion by sound alone — all clear?
Yes, completely clear.

meanings.note: Humble noun form of 待たせる, used in apologies like お待たせしました.

examples.text: 大変お待たせいたしました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for waiting.

examples.text: お待たせしてすみません。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Compound ichidan verb formed from する + すぎる.

examples.text: 最近働きすぎています。
examples.trans: I've been working too much lately.

examples.text: 心配しすぎないでください。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Core adverb in set greetings like よろしくお願いします and どうぞよろしく.
With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 大丈夫ですよ、もともと人前でしゃべるのは得意ですから。
examples.trans: Don't worry — speaking in front of an audience has always been my strong suit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.
I see that to be seen.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

examples.text: こう見えてわたくし、英会話教材のセールスでトップだったんですよ。
examples.trans: Believe it or not, I used to be the number-one salesman of English conversation sets!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'sales'.

examples.text: これからセールスに行きます。
examples.trans: I'm going out on sales calls now.

examples.text: セールスの仕事は大変です。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'top'.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

examples.text: 再生されるたびに新鮮で、いわば永遠の処女でございます。
examples.trans: Every time the tape is played I am fresh and alive—in other words, I am an eternal virgin.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。
この小道具を有効に使いたいと思います。吹いてみてください。
examples.trans: Let's put this prop to brilliant use — please try giving it a blow.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.trans: Let's put this prop to brilliant use — please try giving it a blow.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。
この小道具を有効に使いたいと思います。吹いてみてください。
examples.trans: Let's put this prop to brilliant use — please try giving it a blow.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; takes を or と.

examples.text: 季節の変化を感じます。
examples.trans: I feel the change of seasons.

examples.text: 少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
examples.trans: You may feel it's a little expensive.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。
もっと感じてきたなという時には二回。もうこれはたまらないなという時には三回。
examples.trans: When you feel even more, blow twice—and when you simply cannot bear it anymore, three times.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: もっと感じてきたなという時には二回。もうこれはたまらないなという時には三回。
examples.trans: When you feel even more, blow twice—and when you simply cannot bear it anymore, three times.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: 見ている方があなたの感じ方の度合いを知ることができるんですね。よろしいですね？
examples.trans: That way viewers can tell the exact degree of your emotion by sound alone — all clear?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
